resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 supported. Aramco announced (30 Jun 2024) that the MGS Phase 3 expansion will raise total capacity by an additional 3.15 bscfd 'by 2028' via ~4,000 km of new pipelines and 17 compression trains; construction commenced Q2 2024, completion targeted Q4 2028. OGJ (Sinopec unit $1.4bn MGS-3 pipeline package) is an independent trade origin covering the specific pipeline contract; SPA (official Saudi Press Agency) and World Oil reprint the Aramco award release. The '2028' token is explicit in all three. Original current_ref (aramco.com $25bn contract-awards page) timed out on verification; replaced. No value contradiction.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia supported. The Master Gas System delivers natural gas to customers across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia; the MGS Phase 3 expansion pipelines are entirely domestic (Jafurah field to the national network). SPA is the official Saudi government source; OGJ independently confirms the MGS-3 pipeline is in Saudi Arabia. Both verified for 'Master Gas System' / Saudi context. No contradiction.

Owner1=Aramco 100% supported. The Master Gas System is Aramco's own network; the Phase 3 expansion contracts (incl. the Sinopec-unit MGS-3 pipeline package) were awarded by Aramco, which owns and operates the system. SPA (official) and OGJ (independent trade, pipeline-specific) plus World Oil all attribute ownership to Aramco; all verified for 'Master Gas System'/'Aramco'. Original current_ref MEED link (aramco-selects-contractors-for-master-gas-system-expansion) and aramco.com page were dead/timed out; replaced. No contradiction.
